name: Flutter

beginner.content:
What is Flutter?

• Flutter is Google's open-source UI toolkit for building natively compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase.
• It uses the Dart programming language and renders every pixel itself via the Skia/Impeller graphics engine, instead of relying on native platform widgets - which is why a Flutter app looks and behaves identically on Android and iOS.
• Everything in Flutter is a Widget - text, padding, buttons, even the whole app itself. Widgets are composed together to build the UI, and Flutter rebuilds only the parts of the widget tree that actually change.

Why Flutter?

1. Single Codebase: Write once, deploy to Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
2. Hot Reload: See code changes reflected in the running app in under a second, without losing app state.
3. Native Performance: Compiles to native ARM/Intel machine code (AOT) for release builds - no JavaScript bridge like some cross-platform frameworks.
4. Rich Widget Library: Material Design (Android-style) and Cupertino (iOS-style) widgets ship out of the box.

intermediate.content:
StatelessWidget vs StatefulWidget

• StatelessWidget: immutable - once built, it never changes. Use it for UI that doesn't depend on any mutable state (e.g. a static label, an icon).
• StatefulWidget: paired with a State object that CAN change over the widget's lifetime. Calling setState() tells Flutter "something changed, rebuild me" - Flutter then efficiently re-renders only the affected subtree.

beginner.content:
Building Layouts with Widgets

Flutter layout is built by composing widgets. The two most fundamental layout widgets are:
• Row - arranges children horizontally.
• Column - arranges children vertically.

Other common layout widgets: Container (box model - padding, margin, decoration), Stack (overlapping children), Expanded/Flexible (share available space), ListView (scrollable list).

Why State Management?

setState() works fine for small, local state, but it doesn't scale: it can't share state between distant widgets without passing data down through many constructors ("prop drilling"). Provider is one of the most common Flutter state-management packages - it makes an object available to any widget below it in the tree, and rebuilds only the widgets that actually read that object.

intermediate.content:
context.watch() vs context.read()

• context.watch<T>(): subscribes this widget to rebuilds whenever T changes - use it inside build().
• context.read<T>(): reads the value once without subscribing to rebuilds - use it inside callbacks (onPressed, etc.) where you don't need the widget itself to rebuild.

beginner.content:
Navigating Between Screens

Flutter manages screens with a stack of routes via the Navigator widget. Navigator.push() adds a new screen on top of the stack; Navigator.pop() removes the current screen and returns to the previous one.

Calling a REST API

The http package makes network requests, which are inherently asynchronous (they return a Future). FutureBuilder is a widget that rebuilds itself based on the state of a Future - loading, error, or data.

cheatNotes: Widget - The basic building block of every Flutter UI element
StatelessWidget - Immutable widget with no internal mutable state
StatefulWidget - Widget backed by a State object that can change via setState()
setState() - Notifies Flutter to rebuild a StatefulWidget subtree
BuildContext - Handle to a widget's location in the widget tree
Scaffold - Provides the basic Material Design visual layout (AppBar, body, FAB)
Row / Column - Arrange children horizontally / vertically
Container - Box-model widget for padding, margin, decoration, sizing
Expanded / Flexible - Make a child fill or share available space in a Row/Column
ListView.builder - Efficiently builds a long/infinite scrollable list on demand
Hot Reload - Injects updated code into a running app in under a second
Hot Restart - Restarts the app fresh, resetting all state
pubspec.yaml - Declares dependencies, assets, and fonts for a Flutter project
MaterialApp / CupertinoApp - Root widget providing Android / iOS style theming
Navigator.push() / pop() - Push a new route onto / pop the top route off the stack
Provider - Popular package for sharing and rebuilding on state changes
ChangeNotifier - Class that can notify listeners when its data changes
context.watch<T>() - Subscribes to rebuilds when T changes (used in build())
context.read<T>() - Reads T once without subscribing (used in callbacks)
Future / async / await - Dart's building blocks for asynchronous code
FutureBuilder - Rebuilds UI based on a Future's loading/error/data state
StreamBuilder - Rebuilds UI based on events from a Stream
const constructor - Marks a widget as compile-time constant for better performance
Key - Identifies widgets across rebuilds, important for list item state
